summary: Griffith Island Light, placed in operation 27 December 1858 off Cape Commodore: keepers Hill and Boyd, the 1922 loss of keeper George Bennett, automated 1924, private island today.

lens.note: Fourth-order lens installed in 1928, replacing a seventh-order lens (LighthouseFriends, quoting the Lake Carriers' Association 1928 report); the first light was a third-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: Finished 1857 with a temporary light (LighthouseFriends). Heights differ: 19.5 m above ground (Coast Guard list), about 20 m / 65 ft (Lighthouse Directory), 85 ft (LighthouseFriends), 50 ft to the platform (Darius Smith, 1876, as quoted by LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: one-and-a-half-storey stone dwelling (1-story limestone house per Lighthouse Directory)
structures.note: Abandoned since 1955 and collapsing into ruins (Lighthouse Directory)

staffing.note: Acetylene apparatus automated the light before the 1924 season (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Island privately owned by the Griffith Island Club since 1973, except the light's parcel; site and tower closed; accessible only by boat (Lighthouse Directory). LighthouseFriends says grounds open, tower closed

events.note: John Brown, builder from Thorold, contracted for eleven lighthouses; six built, the Imperial Towers
Foundations prepared and limestone quarried; the season's setback: two steamers and a schooner wrecked and much timber lost, location not given
Tower and one-and-a-half-storey dwelling finished; temporary light set on the tower while the lantern was late
Placed in operation 27 December 1858: fixed white light from a third-order Fresnel lens; LighthouseFriends calls it the third of the six Imperial Towers formally placed in operation
Inspection by Darius Smith, Superintendent of Lights above Montreal; keeper Hill described as old and not very strong, wanting to be superannuated
Keeper Vesey C. Hill superannuated at 66 on 27 April 1881; Garrett Washington Patterson head keeper from 1881
William S. Boyd head keeper from 1889 to 1922, the longest tenure on the island
Duplex lamp replaced by a 55 mm. Diamond vapour installation and adjustable brass stand (Department of Marine report for the fiscal year ended 31 March 1909, printed 1910)
George H. Bennett head keeper in 1922; Frederick W. Thornley head keeper 1922 to 1923

Keeper George H. Bennett, who had lost a leg in World War I, left the south-side dock on 13 December 1922 for the light by boat, was swept out into Georgian Bay and perished; the Evening Star reported him missing in a small motorboat
Acetylene apparatus automated the light before the opening of the 1924 season
Fourth-order lens replaced a seventh-order lens, as noted in the Lake Carriers' Association annual report for 1928 (quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Island, except the light's parcel, privately owned by the Griffith Island Club from 1973

notes_for_editor: Heights and focal plane disagree across sources: LighthouseFriends gives a tower of 85 ft and a focal plane of 130 ft (39.6 m) above the bay, and quotes Darius Smith (1876) at 50 ft to the platform; the Lighthouse Directory gives approx 20 m (65 ft) and a focal plane of 31 m (102 ft); the Coast Guard list gives 19.5 m and 31.3 m. The record's 31.3 m and 19.5 m are kept. The story reports the spread and does not choose. The first light date 27 December 1858 is LighthouseFriends; the Lighthouse Directory gives 1858 only. The record's event 'built 1858' may be the Lighthouse Directory's date for the tower; LighthouseFriends says the tower was finished in 1857. Grounds: LighthouseFriends says 'Grounds open, tower closed' in its visitor information, while the Lighthouse Directory says 'Site and tower closed' and gives the site manager as Griffith Island Club. The record's grounds_open is set to false; the story states both. Ordering conflict with the Christian Island page: LighthouseFriends' Christian Island page calls Christian Island the last of the six Imperial Towers to be officially activated (1 May 1859), while the Griffith Island page calls Griffith the third to be formally placed in operation (27 December 1858). Both are LighthouseFriends statements; the Christian story says the plaque calls it the first to be completed. A human should decide which order to print. Keepers: names and years come from the LighthouseFriends head-keeper line; narrative confirms Frame, Hill, Boyd, Bennett and Thornley; Patterson (1881-1889) is only in the line, so he is cited to LighthouseFriends with no narrative. 'Sarah was born in Africa' is LighthouseFriends's own statement with no source given; the editor may want a census check or may drop the line. The Department of Marine tables in the corpus name 'W. S. Boyd' at Griffith Island in 1905 and 1912 (OCR column blocks; identifiers 1906v40i9p21_0345 scan 333, 1912v46i14p21_0847 scan 254); these were not cited because the columns could not be read reliably, and the page images should be checked. Bennett 1922: LighthouseFriends gives the detail (lost a leg in WWI, left dock 13 Dec 1922, swept out and perished) and cites the Owosso Argus-Press of 16 December 1922, which was not read. The Evening Star (19 Dec 1922, p. 33) confirms the keeper's disappearance in a small motorboat and the search; its OCR is damaged ('in &' for 'in a') and the paper spells the place 'Griffiths Island'. The rescue search was by the tug Muriel per the Evening Star's damaged text; not cited. The 1856 wreck of two steamers and a schooner is reported by LighthouseFriends without location; the same sentence appears on the Christian Island page. The Commissioners of Public Works reports (1852-53, 1857-58) are not in the corpus and are quoted here only as LighthouseFriends prints them. Newspapers: a broad Chronicling America search for 'Griffith Island' 1858-1930 returned 32 pages, mostly unrelated (no 1858 first-light report was found); only the 1922 Evening Star item is used. The 1922 Marine report (1923v59i5p28_1679, scan 32) lists Griffith island in a station table; not read for detail. Access and safety: the island is private (Griffith Island Club since 1973) and the tower is closed; the story says so and gives no route to land. The Griffith Island Club's reported application for ownership of the light is stated as reported (Lighthouse Directory; LighthouseFriends hedges with 'reportedly'); not verified.
